title: Enumerations and valid states
goal: Name states and explicitly check which transitions are valid.

prerequisites.text: Know if conditions and logical AND/OR.
Map a numeric code to a named value.

terms.title: Enumeration
terms.definition: A type with named integer constants. The enumeration does not validate input for the program.

terms.title: Enumerator
terms.definition: The name of an integer constant, such as OPEN in the example.

terms.title: Transition
terms.definition: A change from the current state to the next state allowed by the task rules.

sections.title: Two questions about a state
paragraphs: A gate receives a code from a controller. Before displaying a state, it needs to know whether that code belongs to the protocol. Skipping a step during a transition is a different kind of mistake.
enum GateState names LOCKED and OPEN. The values 10 and 20 are choices of this protocol. Do not assume that every incoming int automatically becomes a valid state.
In a library, a requested loan can become issued, and an issued loan can become returned. Both state names can belong to the enumeration while their particular transition is still invalid.
State recognition and transition permission answer different questions. A code can be known while the transition to it is forbidden.

sections.title: Names for two gate codes
paragraphs: Read the three gate_label calls and name the branch taken by 10, 20 and 0.
steps: Compare raw with LOCKED and OPEN in the switch. Here the named constants stand for 10 and 20.
Return a label immediately for each known value. The default handles other integers.
The third line unknown is the defined result for an unrecognized code, not a compilation error.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: The typo RETUREND causes an undeclared identifier diagnostic. Compare it with the declared name RETURNED. If the program prints ok for 1 3, inspect the allowed pairs rather than the enum declaration.
An unknown code and a prohibited transition have distinct output. The pair 0 2 yields invalid, while the recognized pair 1 3 yields denied.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Change the last call to gate_label(30). Predict the output. Then identify what additional rule is needed to decide whether LOCKED can change to OPEN.
Build a 3×3 table for the library starter. Rows are current states and columns are target states. Mark only the two allowed cells.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the language constructs used in the worked example.

feedback: Neither named value equals 0. The default branch runs.

selfcheck.prompt: Both codes 1 and 3 are known. What is the result of moving from 1 to 3?
feedback: The codes are recognized. A transition rule is violated.
Returning requires the book to be issued first.

selfcheck.prompt: Explain why checking that a state is known is separate from checking a transition. Suggest one input for each error.
selfcheck.feedback: 0 2 contains an unknown code. 3 2 contains known states but violates a transition rule. The errors call for different remedies.

practice.title: Book issuing and return
practice.task: Read the first line, up to 63 bytes, with two integers for current and target state. Codes 1, 2 and 3 mean requested, issued and returned. Print invalid for malformed input or an unknown code. Print ok for 1 → 2 and 2 → 3, and denied for every other known pair. Input recognition is supplied. Complete can_move.
criteria: Both allowed pairs yield ok. A skipped, reversed or repeated state yields denied.
Unknown codes and malformed input yield invalid. Validate codes before converting to the enum type.
practice.hint: Use && to check both sides of a pair, then combine the two allowed pairs with ||.

steps.action: Mark the allowed cells in the transition table.
steps.why: This shows that repeating 2 → 2 has a defined outcome.

steps.action: Run one case for each of ok, denied and invalid.
steps.why: The two negative results belong to different parts of the contract.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Transfer the approach to a turnstile with codes 10 and 20. Specify outcomes for a repeated state and an unknown code before writing the condition.
criteria: Show a recognized transition and an unknown code on separate examples. Explain your choice of repeat behavior.

teaching.scene: A gate receives numeric codes from an external log. Identify which codes name valid states and which ones must be rejected before checking a transition.

predict.prompt: gate_label receives 10, 20 and 0 in that order. Which switch branch handles each input, and what prints?
predict.answer: 10 matches LOCKED and prints locked. 20 matches OPEN and prints open. No named case matches 0, so default gives unknown.

apply.prompt: For a lending log, compare pairs 2 → 3, 3 → 2 and 9 → 2. How can you distinguish a forbidden transition from an unknown code?
apply.answer: 2 → 3 is permitted and gives ok. 3 → 2 contains known states but is reversed, giving denied. 9 → 2 starts with an unknown code, so it gives invalid.

practice.strategy: Check the input codes against the known set. Mark only the permitted pairs in a transition table and compare both endpoints of each pair.
practice.diagnosis: The starter gives denied for 1 2 and ok for 2 2. It checks equality instead of checking permitted transitions.

syntax.example:
enum RequestState { REQUESTED = 1, ISSUED = 2, RETURNED = 3 };
enum RequestState current = ISSUED;
syntax.explanation: Named enum constants link numbers to states. A switch case matches the numeric value, and default handles other codes.
syntax.mistake: An enum type alone does not validate a number from input. Recognize the code before applying transition rules.
